These tests do not build on Windows. The module is gated `#[cfg(all(test, unix))]` at line 528, so nothing in it is compiled for a Windows target. Within a Unix build `cfg!(windows)` is a compile-target constant that is always false, so `path_entries` returns the `bin` entry and both assertions hold.

I have gated the parsing tests and their helper for linux/macos as suggested in the other comment, since that function is narrower than the module.

The test is already compile-gated by the enclosing `#[cfg(all(test, unix))] mod tests` at `src/client/input.rs:471`; it is never compiled for Windows. The current exact head also passed the repository `check (windows-latest)` job and local Windows-target Clippy, so an additional per-test `#[cfg(unix)]` would be redundant.

this validates `HERDR_SESSION` even when `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` is set and no cli `--session` was passed.

given the documented precedence, the exact socket override should win over `HERDR_SESSION` in that case. this command should use `/tmp/herdr.sock` and ignore the invalid session env:

```bash
HERDR_SOCKET_PATH=/tmp/herdr.sock HERDR_SESSION='bad/name' herdr workspace list
```

please skip `HERDR_SESSION` validation when `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` is present and there is no explicit cli `--session`, and add a regression test for that precedence case.
